note: Position 2 alone, the slide from position 1 with its two notes lit, the same shapes moved to C, then improvising across both. The crossing is named exactly (which string, which notes) instead of as jargon; each block changes position, key or task.

exercise.title: Join positions 1 and 2
exercise.focus: Minor pentatonic · positions 1 → 2 · A then C
exercise.why: Joining positions turns five separate shapes into one neck you can move along mid-phrase.

sections.text: Press Play below to start the metronome. Play position 2 of A minor pentatonic up and down, one note per beat. It starts at the 7th fret, and its ringed {{1}} notes sit on the D and B strings.
Climb position 1 from the low A. On the G string, slide from {{4}} (D, 7th fret) up to {{5}} (E, 9th fret) and finish the climb in position 2. On the way down, slide from {{5}} back to {{4}}.
In C minor pentatonic everything moves up three frets: position 1 starts at the 8th fret, and the slide on the G string goes from {{4}} (F) to {{5}} (G).

Press Play below to start the backing, which switches between Cm7 and Fm7. Improvise across both positions, using the slide on the G string to move between them. Land on {{c}} when Cm7 comes round and on {{f}} when Fm7 comes round.
